dedupe_keys.name: field data and observations of damaged buildings ten weeks after the february 2023 earthquake sequence in turkiye

description: Field Data and Observations of Damaged Buildings Ten Weeks after the February 2023 Earthquake Sequence in Türkiye is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "field recon", published or maintained by Francisco Galvis, Stanford University (stanford.edu). The February 2023 earthquakes in Türkiye constitute one of the largest shaking sequences in recent history that has impacted a significant area and vast number of buildings designed per modern seismic design provisions. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "field recon" project. Keywords: 2023 Türkiye-Syria earthquake, reconnaissance, resilience. Published 2023-11-18. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
